security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel writes sstatus.UXL=1 (UXLEN=32) to switch a task to 32-bit U-mode without first probing that UXLEN=32 is in the hardware's supported set (i.e., that Ssu32xl is present). If the hart only supports Ssu64xl, the write is either ignored or traps, leaving the kernel believing it is running a 32-bit task while UXLEN remains 64 — register width mismatch, address truncation, and signal-frame corruption follow.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_write(CSR_SSTATUS, ...) or __riscv_csr_set(CSR_SSTATUS, SR_UXL) where the UXL=1 path is gated only on CONFIG_COMPAT or elf_flags without an isa-extension probe for ssu32xl
security_spec.summary: sstatus.UXL=1 (32-bit U-mode) must only be written after confirming Ssu32xl hardware support; blind write risks silent UXLEN=64 retention causing privilege-boundary confusion between kernel and 32-bit userspace
